q-ar-ain.label: a or an
q-ar-ain.summary: The choice follows the sound the next word starts with, not its spelling.

q-ar-the.label: When 'the' is needed
q-ar-the.summary: Superlatives, one-of-a-kind things, rivers, ranges, oceans and ordinals take 'the'.

q-ar-none.label: Where no article belongs
q-ar-none.summary: Abstract and uncountable nouns in general, meals, languages, and most proper nouns take none.

rules.text: Use 'an' before a vowel SOUND and 'a' before a consonant sound. Spelling does not decide it: an hour, an MLA, an honest man; a university, a one-rupee coin, a European.
rules.ok: An hour, a university, an MP.
rules.bad: A hour, an university, a MP.

rules.text: 'The' goes before a superlative, an ordinal, a thing there is only one of, and before rivers, seas, oceans, mountain ranges, deserts and groups of islands. Single mountains and single lakes take none.
rules.ok: The tallest boy, the Ganga, the Himalayas, the sun.
rules.bad: Tallest boy, Ganga is holy, Himalayas are high.

rules.text: 'The' also marks a noun already known from the situation or mentioned before, and it makes a singular noun stand for its whole class: the tiger is disappearing.
rules.ok: I bought a book. The book was torn.
rules.bad: I bought a book. A book was torn.

rules.text: No article before an abstract or uncountable noun used in general (honesty, advice, information, furniture), before meals, languages, games, most diseases, and before a proper noun; add 'the' only when the noun is narrowed down.
rules.ok: Honesty pays. He plays cricket after lunch.
rules.bad: The honesty pays. He plays the cricket after the lunch.

rules.text: In 'the more ... the more' and 'the + adjective' for a whole class (the poor, the blind), 'the' is required. One article serves two nouns of the same person or thing, but two are needed for two different ones.
rules.ok: The more he earns, the less he saves. A black and a white shirt (two shirts).
rules.bad: More he earns, less he saves.

q-ar-ain.cue: A blank before a noun or adjective, with 'a' and 'an' among the options.
q-ar-ain.standard: Say the next word aloud. If it begins with a vowel sound, use 'an'; otherwise 'a'.
q-ar-ain.fast: Test the first sound, not the first letter: h in 'hour' is silent, u in 'university' sounds like 'yoo'.
q-ar-ain.eliminate: Drop 'the' and the blank option first if the noun is being introduced for the first time.
traps: Words beginning with a silent h (hour, honour, heir) take 'an'.
Words beginning with a 'yoo' or 'wun' sound (university, European, one) take 'a'.
Single letters and abbreviations go by sound: an MLA, an FIR, a UPSC notification.

q-ar-the.cue: A blank before a superlative, an ordinal, a river or range, or a noun mentioned earlier.
q-ar-the.standard: Ask whether the noun is one of a kind, already known, or the best or first of something. If yes, use 'the'.
q-ar-the.fast: Superlative or ordinal in the phrase means 'the'.
q-ar-the.eliminate: If the noun is being met for the first time and is countable and singular, 'the' is usually wrong.
traps: Rivers and ranges take 'the' but single peaks and lakes do not.
'The' before a second mention is easy to drop in a long sentence.

q-ar-none.cue: A blank before an abstract noun, a meal, a language or a game, with 'no article' among the options.
q-ar-none.standard: Ask whether the noun is being used in general. If it is, leave it bare.
q-ar-none.fast: Abstract noun used generally, meal, language or game: no article.
q-ar-none.eliminate: Cross out 'the' unless the sentence narrows the noun down with a phrase or clause.
traps: 'Advice', 'information', 'furniture' and 'luggage' are uncountable and take no 'a'.
'The' returns as soon as the noun is specified: the advice he gave me.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The meeting lasted ___ hour and a half.
practice.why: 'Hour' begins with a vowel sound because the h is silent, so it takes 'an'.

a.note: 'A hour' goes by the letter h instead of the sound; the h in 'hour' is not pronounced.

c.note: 'The hour' would point to one particular hour already known, which the sentence does not.

d.note: A singular countable noun being introduced needs an article.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
She has joined ___ university in Pune.
practice.why: 'University' begins with a 'yoo' sound, which is a consonant sound, so it takes 'a'.

a.note: 'An university' goes by the vowel letter u; the word is pronounced 'yoo-niversity'.

c.note: 'The university' would mean a particular one already known to the listener.

d.note: A singular countable noun needs an article here.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
He filed ___ FIR at the police station.
practice.why: The abbreviation FIR is read as 'ef-eye-ar', which begins with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an'.

a.note: 'A FIR' goes by the letter F; read aloud, the letter begins with the vowel sound 'ef'.

c.note: 'The FIR' would refer to one already mentioned; here it is being filed for the first time.

d.note: A singular countable noun needs an article here.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
He is ___ tallest boy in the class.
practice.why: A superlative singles out one person, so it takes 'the'.

a.note: 'A tallest' is impossible: a superlative cannot be one of several.

b.note: 'An tallest' is wrong in both the article and the sound.

d.note: Leaving out the article before a superlative is a common slip; English requires 'the'.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
___ Ganga rises in the Himalayas.
practice.why: Rivers take 'the', as do mountain ranges, seas and oceans.

a.note: 'A Ganga' would make the river one of several of that name.

b.note: 'An Ganga' is wrong in both the article and the sound.

d.note: Dropping the article before a river name is common in speech, but a river takes 'the'.

practice.text:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
I bought a dictionary yesterday / but dictionary was missing / twenty pages / in the middle.
practice.why: At the second mention the noun is already known, so it needs 'the dictionary'.

a.note: 'A dictionary' is right for the first mention of a countable noun.

c.note: 'Twenty pages' is a plural count and needs no article.

d.note: 'In the middle' is a fixed phrase and is correct.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
___ honesty is the best policy in the long run.
practice.why: An abstract noun used in general takes no article.

a.note: 'A honesty' is impossible: honesty is uncountable.

b.note: 'An honesty' is impossible for the same reason.

c.note: 'The honesty' would point to one particular person's honesty, which the sentence does not do.

practice.text:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
He gave me / a very useful advice / about the examination / last evening.
practice.why: 'Advice' is uncountable, so it cannot take 'a'; it should be 'very useful advice' or 'a very useful piece of advice'.

a.note: 'He gave me' is a correct main clause.

c.note: 'About the examination' points to a known examination and is correct.

d.note: 'Last evening' is a correct phrase of time.

practice.text:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:
[[The more you read the more]] you understand.
options: The more you read, the more
practice.why: Both halves of the 'the more ... the more' pattern keep 'the'.

b.note: Dropping both articles is the commonest form of this error; the pattern needs 'the' twice.

c.note: The second half has lost its 'the'.

d.note: The first half has lost its 'the'.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
We had ___ lunch at a small place near the office.
practice.why: Names of meals take no article when they mean the meal in general.

a.note: 'A lunch' is used only when the meal is described as an event, as in 'a lunch in his honour'.

b.note: 'The lunch' would point to one particular meal already known.

d.note: 'An lunch' is wrong in both the article and the sound.
